stem: That contractor's compliance team also requires the AWS CloudHSM deployment to keep operating if an entire Availability Zone becomes unavailable, and requires the application to authenticate to the HSMs using the same PKCS #11 interface it already uses on premises. Which TWO design choices meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Create the CloudHSM cluster with HSMs spread across at least two Availability Zones
Create a single HSM in one Availability Zone and rely on AWS KMS as a warm standby for it
Put an AWS KMS custom key store in front of the cluster so the application calls KMS APIs instead
Integrate the application with the cluster using the CloudHSM PKCS #11 library
Authenticate the application to the cluster using only the CloudHSM JCE provider

rationale: Spreading a CloudHSM cluster's HSMs across at least two Availability Zones is exactly how AWS CloudHSM achieves redundancy and high availability, and the cluster automatically load-balances operations across every HSM it contains. Integrating the application through the CloudHSM PKCS #11 library preserves the same interface the application already uses on premises. A single HSM in one Availability Zone has no redundancy, and AWS KMS cannot act as a standby for a CloudHSM cluster since they are separate services with separate key material. Placing an AWS KMS custom key store in front of the cluster means the application talks to the KMS API, not PKCS #11, directly against the HSMs, so it does not preserve the required interface. The JCE provider is a Java-specific interface, not the PKCS #11 interface the application already depends on.
